messages.author: 644e1c01c3c42210
messages.subject: Re: [MplusAutomation] MonteCarlo in Mplusautomation
parts:
Dear Zahra,

If you want the individual LL values, you need to run each replication individually as an analysis and extract the results using readModels. The MONTECARLO syntax you have used will take the replications in your list and run each, then compile summary statistics such as mean LL, MSE, etc. (this is a feature of Mplus). Attached is an example of how to run each replication separately, building on the parallel features in R so that you can run as many models simultaneously as you have cores available. Hope this helps! This was written before Josh’s useful mplusModeler was built into the package, so some of the code could be further streamlined to integrate the inline use of Mplus.

Best,
Michael

Parts of the file I sent are specific to a project I was working on. The general point is to loop over your replications, save the syntax to a file (I use temp files to avoid bloating my file system), run it using runModels, extract the output using readModels, and store all of the results into a structure for tabulation and comparison.
